findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||, blocking team admins
findings.body: The permission check computes `isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId))`. This only passes for a user who is simultaneously a team admin AND a team owner, so regular team admins (who are not owners) get FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests to team bookings. This should be an OR: `isTeamAdmin(...) || isTeamOwner(...)`.

findings.title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive and easily bypassed
findings.body: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` entries are lowercased, but the incoming guest email is compared without lowercasing: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. A blacklisted address like `spam@example.com` can be added as `Spam@Example.com` and bypass the blacklist entirely. The guest email should be normalized (e.g. `guest.toLowerCase()`) before the comparison (and ideally before the duplicate-attendee comparison too, since email matching against existing attendees is also case-sensitive).

findings.title: No check that the booking is in a valid state before adding guests
findings.body: The handler fetches the booking by id but never checks `booking.status`. Guests can be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings (and past bookings), and both the calendar update (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`) and the emails send an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and method `REQUEST`, re-inviting people to a cancelled event. The handler should reject bookings that are cancelled/rejected (and arguably past).

findings.title: Calendar attendee update uses the requester's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` builds the EventManager with the calling user's credentials. But attendees are allowed to call this endpoint (`isAttendee` passes the permission check), and an attendee typically has no credentials for the organizer's calendar, so `updateCalendarAttendees` will either no-op or update the wrong calendar. The calendar event lives on the organizer's calendar, so the organizer's credentials (already partially loaded via `booking.user.credentials`) should be used.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email-disable settings
findings.body: Every other sender in this file (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, etc.) respects `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` so organizers can disable standard emails via event type metadata. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata parameter and unconditionally emails the organizer, all team members, and all attendees, so guests-added emails are sent even when the event type is configured to suppress standard emails.

findings.title: New-guest detection can fail due to email casing mismatch
findings.body: `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares the raw user input against stored attendee emails. If the entered email differs in case from what was stored, a newly added guest receives the 'existing attendee' AttendeeAddGuestsEmail instead of the AttendeeScheduledEmail with full booking details, and conversely an existing attendee could be mis-classified. Compare case-insensitively.

findings.title: Clicking Add with only the default empty field shows a validation error
findings.body: `multiEmailValue` is initialized to `[""]`, so its length is 1, not 0. If the user opens the dialog and clicks Add without typing anything, `safeParse` fails on the empty string and the user sees the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' error instead of the action being a no-op. Empty strings should be filtered out before the length check and validation.
